findings.text: the reviewed cases pin that the metas decide whether a given document is a record, but no case has the metas naming a plan the filename does not, so the rule this module's docstring states and the landing paragraph repeats has no failing case: with the resolver's plan source moved to the filename (the metas still required for identity) all three reviewed cases pass, and a disagreement case of that shape fails under the mutation and passes on the reviewed revision (two-arm probe, this review's logs/durability-probe.log), so a regression that took the plan from the path would be invisible to the guard.

the read path swallows a composition failure with pass and a comment, where the same fallback logs a warning at serve.py:2103 and reports a record-not-composed finding at doccheck.py:1249, so a read_plan caller receiving a record's own bytes cannot tell an unreadable ledger from a record with no fragments — the hiding the re-review required the other two readers to end, left on the third.

baseline_suite and after_suite hold prose rather than the armed JSON the keys reserve and no baseline arm was run, so the suite-delta reader sees no arms and the added-failure count is left unmeasured (the store's read-time annotation reports the same); the gate logs named under test_logs carry no header, so the revision and command behind the 16-passed claim are unverifiable from the logs alone and had to be re-established by this review's independent re-run.

justifications.durability: the identity half of the resolver is guarded by an observable negative shape — the parked fragment makes ordinary a claim about what was not composed in — and the declared mutation reddens it; the plan-source half has no case, measured with a two-arm probe (logs/durability-probe.log): a resolver that keeps the metas for identity and takes the plan from the filename passes all three reviewed cases, while a disagreement case of that shape fails under that mutation (composing the filename's fragment) and passes on the reviewed revision, so the metas-win rule is carried by construction only.
justifications.evidence: the 16-passed gate was reproduced independently at 16ca61e7 with module-under-test and resolved cwd (logs/gate-at-16ca61e7.log), the negative control's first line repeats the declared mutation verbatim and its log is red with one failure, and the added-failure derivation was falsified with a positive control before its empty result was reported; deductions for the headerless gate logs the manifest names, for baseline_suite and after_suite being prose with no baseline arm run so the no-new-failures delta is asserted rather than logged, and for the pass-unchanged clause, which the landing's own identity rule made unsatisfiable for that file and which the manifest discloses under follow_ons instead.
justifications.fit: the resolver sits in evidence.py beside compose_landed_record with a why-docstring, its normalisation at evidence.py:442 matches the SPA's _refSlug (docs/ui/graph.jsx:12) exactly, no plan, sprint or version identifier appears in code or comments, and the three-reader shape follows the surrounding reader idiom; the deduction is the silent fallback at reckon/mcp.py:1104, which departs from the observability the same fallback carries in serve.py:2103 and doccheck.py:1249.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the three readers share one resolver and read_plan composes, verified in the diff and by the re-run gate; the deduction is that the read path swallows a composition failure silently at reckon/mcp.py:1104 where the two repaired readers say so, leaving the third able to hide fragments exactly as the re-review required the other two not to.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in both commits lies inside the manifest's nine declared paths with nothing outside them, the cumulative evidence record is spliced (six gains, zero losses) rather than rewritten, the reviewed worktree is clean at 16ca61e7, and no plan-state meta line is touched by the documentation commit.
